info.description:
Admin API for Drop: a Drive-like tree where any folder holding a `.drop` descriptor is a publishable drop. Metadata lives in SQL; file bytes live in MinIO.
Every endpoint outside /v1/auth needs a token. Get one from POST /v1/auth/login and send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
info.title: Drop Admin API

get.description: Serves a drop's content by slug. Without a path the drop's entrypoint is returned; with one, that file. A leading `@<seq>` segment pins an older version, so `/d/{slug}/@2/` keeps serving what version 2 published. A private drop answers only for the accounts that may open it — its owner and whoever it is shared with, by session cookie or bearer token — and 404s for everyone else, so the response never reveals that the slug exists.

parameters.description: File inside the drop; defaults to the entrypoint
parameters.name: filepath

get.description: Returns ok when the API process is up.

post.description: Exchanges email and password for an access token and the refresh token that renews it. Rate limited per client address.
Revokes the session behind a refresh token. Answers 204 whether or not the token was recognized: signing out is not a place to learn which tokens are real.
Exchanges a refresh token for a fresh access token. The refresh token itself keeps working until it expires or its session is revoked.

get.description: Returns a drop's metadata and the files it is composed of.

post.description: Creates a drop: a node carrying metadata plus a materialized `.drop` YAML descriptor in object storage.

patch.description: Patches title, visibility, or entrypoint and refreshes the drop's `.drop` descriptor.

post.description: Creates a drop and uploads its files in a single multipart request. Repeat the `file` field once per file. To place files in subdirectories, repeat a `path` field as well — the Nth `path` names the Nth `file` — because RFC 7578 forbids directory information in a part's filename. Everything is validated before any byte is stored, and a failed upload rolls the whole drop back.
post.summary: Create a drop with its files

parameters.description: Relative path for each file, in the same order as `file`
parameters.name: path

parameters.description: Page to open. Inferred when omitted: the only HTML uploaded, whatever its name, or index.html when there are several
parameters.name: entrypoint

parameters.description: Destination folder; defaults to the root
parameters.name: parent

parameters.description: Folder name; defaults to a slug of the title
parameters.name: name

get.description: Returns the drop's publication history, newest first. Each entry carries a URL that keeps serving that snapshot even after later uploads.

post.description: Points the drop's URL back at an earlier snapshot. Nothing is deleted: the history keeps every version, including the one that was current.

get.description: Streams a file stored inside a drop.

post.description: Stores one or more files inside a drop. Send them as multipart/form-data under the `file` field; an existing file of the same name is replaced.

delete.description: Removes one file from a drop.

post.description: Issues a single-use link. There is no public sign-up and no email is sent: the link is returned here, once, and handed over by whatever channel you like. Only its hash is stored.
The invitation carries the email address, so only a name and a password are asked for. Does not sign the new account in — the password just chosen is the one immediately used to log in.
post.summary: Create the account behind a pending invitation

get.description: Lets the acceptance page decide what to show before asking for a password. Answers 410 once the invitation is no longer usable — already accepted, expired, or revoked.
get.summary: Preview an invitation before accepting it

delete.description: Cancels a pending invitation, so its link stops working.

get.description: Lists the direct children of a folder. An empty path lists the root. Returns 409 `is_drop` when the path is a drop — fetch it via /v1/drops instead.

parameters.description: Folder path; empty means the root
parameters.name: path

post.description: Creates a plain organizational folder inside another folder.

delete.description: Deletes the node and everything beneath it, including the stored files of every drop in the subtree.

parameters.description: Path of the node to delete
parameters.name: path

post.description: The one thing an empty instance lets happen; everything else stays behind setupGate until this succeeds. Signs the new administrator in, same as login.
post.summary: Create the organization and its first administrator

get.summary: Report whether this instance still needs its first administrator

get.description: Only the granted nodes themselves, not what is inside them — the same way Drive shows the shared folder rather than every file under it.
get.summary: List what other people have shared with the caller

get.description: Candidates excludes the node's owner and any disabled account, the same filter the admin UI applies before offering a share dialog.
get.summary: List who has access to a node, and who could still be given some

post.description: Sharing again at a different level changes it in place rather than erroring: exactly one grant exists per (node, user).
post.summary: Grant or update a user's access to a node

delete.description: The owner may revoke any grant; an editor may only revoke grants they personally created.
delete.summary: Revoke a user's access to a node

delete.description: Soft-deletes the account and revokes its sessions. The address becomes free to invite again.

patch.description: Disabling also revokes the user's sessions, so it takes effect at once rather than whenever their access token expires.

access.description:
Access is what the caller may do with it: owner, editor or viewer. The
interface hides the actions it does not cover.

entrypoint_missing.description:
EntrypointMissing marks a drop whose entrypoint names no file it holds.
Its URL answers 404 until a page by that name arrives, or the metadata
is pointed at one that exists.

owner.description:
Owner is whose drive it lives in. A path only identifies a node together
with this, since every user has their own tree.

url.description:
URL is where the drop can be opened. Serving it is subject to
visibility: a private drop answers there only for the accounts that may
open it, and 404s for everyone else.

versions.description: Versions is the publication history, newest first.

version.description:
Version is the sequence number of the snapshot currently published: 1 on
first upload, and one more each time the drop is uploaded again.

generated.description:
Generated marks a file the system maintains — the ".drop" descriptor.
It can be listed and read, but not written or deleted through the API.

owner.description:
Owner is whose drive it lives in. A path only identifies a node together
with this, since every user has their own tree.

created_by_id.description:
CreatedByID is who granted it, which is what lets an editor tell their
own grants apart from the owner's.

access.description: Access is what the grant allows: viewer or editor.

owner.description:
Owner is whose drive it lives in. A path only identifies a node together
with this, since every user has their own tree.

owner_name.description:
OwnerName and OwnerEmail identify whose drive it lives in, because a
path alone says nothing about that.

current.description: Current marks the version served at the drop's own URL.

url.description: URL pins this snapshot, and keeps working after later uploads.
URL is the link to hand over. No email is sent in this version.
